title: NexaLogix: Onboarding & Activation Workshop
summary: Kickoff/activation workshop covering NexaLogix pilot scope, networking (VPC vs hosted), security/KMS requirements, SLA targets, and next steps to start pilot week of Oct 20. Action items assigned for security docs, pricing, and initial benchmark plan.
topics: Networking options: Hosted API vs VPC/private deployment
Security controls: KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO/SAML
Rollout timeline and immediate next steps
next_steps: Ari to send tailored security pack + SOC2 summary (link) — due 2026-10-15
Liam to share benchmark harness template and suggested test prompts — due 2026-10-16
Customer to confirm pilot start window (prefer week of Oct 20) — customer reply by 2026-10-14
Schedule technical pilot kickoff (SE + customer infra) — target 2026-10-19

Liam O'Neill: Provide benchmark harness, suggested payload sizes, and 1-2 test scripts — due 2026-10-16
Rita Sol (NexaLogix): Share current KMS provider details and compliance constraints — due 2026-10-14

meeting_header:
Date: 2026-10-13 | Time: 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Ari Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Maya Rao (Redwood CSM), Elena Park (NexaLogix Head of ML), Devon Harper (NexaLogix Platform), Rita Sol (NexaLogix Security), Tomás Alvarez (NexaLogix IT Ops)
transcript:
[00:00] Ari Chen: Hey everyone — thanks for joining, we really appreciate you carving time today. Quick roll call, then we'll go into the proposed pilot scope and the networking/security checklist.
[00:15] Elena Park: Hi Ari hi team — Elena here. Good to be on, excited to get this moving.
[00:25] Liam O'Neill: Liam here from Redwood engineering, I'll be running the tech bits, hi all.
[00:32] Devon Harper: Devon, platform eng for NexaLogix. Quick note we have an incident window Friday afternoon so prefer weekdays early.
[00:42] Maya Rao: Maya, CSM, I'll own runbook and success criteria.
[00:48] Tomás Alvarez: Tomás in IT Ops, I'll be the network point.
[00:53] Rita Sol: Rita, security. I'll mainly focus on KMS and audit requirements.
[01:05] Ari Chen: Great. Agenda — pilot scope (what we ship and measure), networking options (hosted vs VPC), security integrations (KMS/HSM, SSO), SLAs/observability, and next steps. Any adjustments?
[01:20] Elena Park: Sounds good. Our internal goals: evaluate latency for 2k context LLM completions and validate that we can keep PII out of logs.
[01:33] Ari Chen: Perfect. We'll plan a 2-week pilot, first week is integration & small scale tests, second week stress tests and benchmarks.
[01:44] Liam O'Neill: For the 2k context the runtime we use will need to pick quant profiles, that's fine. We'll provide a benchmark harness — note: if you push for batch sizes >16 we'll talk cost implications.
[01:58] Devon Harper: On cost — do you have an estimate for dedicated vs hosted for our expected 2M tokens/month?
[02:06] Ari Chen: Yes I'll send a TCO compare — short version: hosted lowers ops overhead but dedicated gives predictable latency and can be cheaper at scale depending on commit. I'll include an example calc in the pricing sheet.
[02:20] Rita Sol: Security wise we need KMS integration with our Vault HSM and audit events sent to our SIEM. Do you support customer-managed keys?
[02:31] Liam O'Neill: We do support KMS and HSM integrations for our Private deployments and Dedicated with VPC. For Hosted API we offer envelope encryption and a bring-your-own-key option via KMS federation in some regions — Liam stumbles on words 'KMS federation' sometimes transcribed as 'KMS free nation' — apologies, that's just the auto transcriber.
[02:55] Rita Sol: Okay we'll need the docs on that. Also certificate renewal flow for peering?
[03:03] Tomás Alvarez: And IP ranges for allowlist, we need to lock down firewall rules.
[03:09] Ari Chen: We'll provide an allowlist and VPC peering guide — link to docs: https://redwood.ai/docs/vpc-peering (note: link share placeholder).
[03:22] Elena Park: Our compliance team will want SOC2 + ISO stuff up front — do you have a summary pack?
[03:29] Maya Rao: Yes, Ari will share the security pack and SOC2 summary, plus we can provide the audit log retention options.
[03:36] Elena Park: Great. For pilot success criteria — here's what we care about: median latency under 150ms for single token generation at typical payloads, 99th under 400ms, no PII in persisted logs, model quality thresholds defined by our sample prompts.
[03:50] Ari Chen: Noted, Maya will draft success criteria doc and we'll align on threshold numbers.
[03:57] Liam O'Neill: Quick tech note — latencies depend on batching and prefix cache. For low-latency SLOs we'll suggest conservative batch sizes and enable prefix KV caching for repeated prompts. Also quantization profile: we'll recommend int8 for the initial pilot on Dedicated.
[04:20] Devon Harper: Does Redwood support auto-fallback if a Dedicated cluster is overloaded? We need graceful degradation.
[04:28] Liam O'Neill: Yes — routing policies can fallback to a compatible hosted variant; we'll show how to set policy to prefer Dedicated then failover to Hosted with reduced context length.
[04:40] Tomás Alvarez: Peering question — are there cross-account IAM pieces or do we do VPC peering only?
[04:47] Ari Chen: Varies by deployment; for Private deployments it's customer-controlled, for Dedicated we do IAM roles plus allowlist. We'll include the exact flow in the network runbook.
[04:58] Rita Sol: Can you confirm retention windows? We want raw transcript/token-level logs not retained by default for compliance.
[05:06] Maya Rao: By default hosted logs are retained 30 days, but Dedicated/Private can configure retention to 0 or ship logs to your SIEM. We'll document options.
[05:18] Elena Park: On-the-ground stakeholders: product (Elena), infra (Devon), security (Rita), and Ops (Tomás). We expect two sprints to be able to validate pilot results.
[05:29] Ari Chen: Sounds sensible. Proposed timeline: integration week starting Oct 20, bench week Oct 27 — does that work?
[05:36] Devon Harper: Oct 20 works on our side.
[05:39] Elena Park: Yes, Oct 20 ok.
[05:41] Ari Chen: Great. Now let's walk through the integration checklist — Liam, can you take the team through the minimal infra steps?
[05:49] Liam O'Neill: Sure — Step 1: decide deployment mode (Hosted API for fastest path, Dedicated for capacity predictability, Private for air-gapped/regulatory). Step 2: for VPC/Dedicated we'll need CIDR, peering contact, firewall rules. Step 3: KMS/HSM details if you want customer-managed keys. Step 4: test creds and service account for benchmark harness.
[06:10] Tomás Alvarez: On step 2 — we use overlapping CIDR with some partners, we might prefer private connect; is private connect an option?
[06:18] Liam O'Neill: We offer VPC peering and also options via PrivateLink/Direct Connect in some clouds — we'll capture specifics for your cloud vendor in the runbook.
[06:28] Rita Sol: For KMS we use HashiCorp Vault with an HSM backend, we'll send the integration details.
[06:35] Liam O'Neill: Perfect — we have a Vault guide; sometimes there's small tweaks for rotation and envelope keys.
[06:42] Elena Park: About model versions — can we pin a version and replicate exact config to avoid drift between pilot and prod?
[06:50] Maya Rao: Yes, our rollout supports pinning model versions and configs; we also support canary rollouts and automatic fallback if quality regresses.
[06:59] Devon Harper: We want to run a quality regression check with 500 prompt pairs across the sample set — can Redwood tie evals to rollouts?
[07:09] Liam O'Neill: Absolutely. Our eval dashboard can run prompt sets, compare outputs, and flag regressions as part of the rollout policy. We'll show that in the console demo.
[07:20] Ari Chen: I know there was a mention of competitor comparisons in your RFP — are there particular red flags you saw?
[07:28] Elena Park: A few — CloudAI had opaque pricing and inconsistent latency across zones; InferBase had good perf but limited security controls. We're testing to decide between more managed vs more control.
[07:41] Ari Chen: Understood. We'll surface where Redwood fits: more production controls and visibility while keeping a fast path via Hosted.
[07:50] Liam O'Neill: Quick demo note — console has token-level breakdowns, per-route latency and cost graphs, and an eval view. Not a full demo today but we'll send links/screencap recording if you'd like.
[08:05] Elena Park: Please send that. Also can we get a sample dashboard export to share with execs?
[08:12] Maya Rao: I'll include a sample export in the follow-up.
[08:17] Tomás Alvarez: On logging — we need the audit logs to include user principal and request ID to tie back to our SIEM.
[08:25] Liam O'Neill: We'll confirm the schema but yes request ID and token-level meta are supported and can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[08:34] Rita Sol: Any mandatory certifications for Private deployments?
[08:38] Ari Chen: For Private we support SOC2 and can work with your compliance team; ISO availability varies by region — we'll include specifics in the security pack.
[08:49] Elena Park: For performance we'll prioritize median p50 and p95, then look at cost per token.
[08:56] Liam O'Neill: One more thing — prefix caching and dedupe of repeated prefixes can dramatically reduce token costs for chatty workflows. If your workload has repeated system prompts we can auto-cache.
[09:12] Devon Harper: Our workload does have repeated templates; good to know.
[09:16] Ari Chen: Alright let's capture immediate deliverables — (1) security pack + SOC2 summary, (2) pricing + TCO compare, (3) benchmark harness + test scripts, (4) pilot success criteria doc. We'll assign owners after this.
[09:31] Maya Rao: I'll own the success criteria doc and coordinate stakeholder sign-off.
[09:36] Ari Chen: Great — who's best on the Nexa side for the firewall and peering info?
[09:40] Tomás Alvarez: I'll handle the firewall and peering details.
[09:44] Devon Harper: I'll run the internal bench and share resource availability.
[09:48] Elena Park: I'll coordinate sample prompts and quality metrics.
[09:52] Rita Sol: I'll consolidate security constraints and KMS details.
[09:55] Ari Chen: Perfect. Any blockers we should call out now?
[10:00] Rita Sol: We need to validate the KMS HSM rotation policy and confirm no customer secrets are stored in Redwood logs.
[10:08] Liam O'Neill: We can confirm retention and show how to forward logs to your SIEM — we'll include that in the security pack.
[10:15] Devon Harper: Also curious about burst capacity if we exceed Dedicated baseline.
[10:20] Ari Chen: There's a burst option for Dedicated and auto-scaling policies, but exact SLAs vary by commit. I'll include the options in the commercial sheet.
[10:32] Elena Park: One small ask — can you provide a checklist we can pass to our infra team to prepare for Oct 20?
[10:38] Maya Rao: Yes I'll attach a one-page infra checklist with required artifacts and sample commands.
[10:45] Ari Chen: We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the technical pilot kickoff tentatively Oct 19 and a firm start Oct 20 once you confirm.
[10:55] Tomás Alvarez: Can we get the allowlist ranges before we start? We need to add them to the firewall change window.
[11:02] Liam O'Neill: We'll send the allowlist and peering range; expect that in the next 24 hours.
[11:10] Elena Park: For the benchmark harness — could you include both synthetic workload and a small sample of redacted real prompts?
[11:18] Liam O'Neill: Yes, we recommend redacting PII on your side then share; we can provide guidance on safe redaction.
[11:25] Rita Sol: We'll prepare a redaction script and share.
[11:30] Ari Chen: Awesome. Quick recap — send security pack & SOC2, pricing/TCO, benchmark harness, infra checklist, and schedule pilot kickoff. Any other items?
[11:39] Elena Park: No, that's it from me.
[11:42] Devon Harper: All good.
[11:44] Tomás Alvarez: Fine here.
[11:46] Maya Rao: I'll create the success criteria doc and circulate a draft by Friday.
[11:52] Ari Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in writing with all items and links. End call.
[48:00] END TRANSCRIPT
